newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slide on profit-taking at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slide on profit-taking at close.

text.p: Mexican stocks revived temporarily on encouraging industrial output figures but slumped at the close on Monday after profit-taking resumed, traders said.

"Stocks were on offer at the close with more profits taken, but I still like the market because it's gathering strength to chalk up further gains," said Arturo Lopez, trader at the Arka brokerage. "Industrial output figures helped a bit."
The blue chip IPC index closed 18.91 points down, or 0.60 percent, at 3,366.22.
Mexico's Finance Ministry released industrial activity data for September, which were 14 percent up on year-ago figures, compared to average expectations of 11.57 percent MXAAP.
Volume was 117.4 million shares traded, but four cross trades alone accounted for some 33 million.
Analysts put the relatively slow trade down to foreign investors staying in the U.S. markets.
"Those who've taken positions here are not going to move, and we see just same-day buy-sell trading in Mexico," said an equity analyst.
"Dealers are taking advantage of returns on the Dow Jones, so volume is thin here," he added.
On the broad market, 106 stocks were traded in total, of which losers outnumbered gainers by 56 to 31.
Steelmakers Tamsa were notable gainers, up 4.90 pesos at 107.00.

Market heavyweight Telmex was among the losers, down 50 centavos at 12.04 pesos, while its ADRs ended off 7/8 at 30-3/8. Another blue chip loser was glassmaker Vitro, which ended down 76 centavos at 14.74 pesos.
Technical analysts meanwhile said the IPC had rebounded close to support at 3,350 points, and could thus trace a double bottom and gain thereafter.
Dealers said Monday evening's primary Cetes auction barely affected trade as rates were expected to change marginally.
A Reuters survey of money traders showed an average forecast of 29.87 percent for the bellwether 28-day rate, or two basis points below last week's auction.
